paragraphs.text: Before booking a hotel or choosing a restaurant, most of us now read online reviews. They can be genuinely helpful, but I have become much more cautious about them than I used to be.

The first problem is that people who write reviews are not typical customers. Those who had an average experience rarely bother, so reviews tend to come from people who were either delighted or furious. The picture they give is therefore more extreme than reality.
Fake reviews are a second concern. Some businesses pay for positive comments, and although the large websites say they remove these, I doubt that they catch them all.

None of this means reviews should be ignored. My own approach is to look for patterns rather than individual comments. If twenty different people mention slow service, it is probably true; if one person describes a disaster, it may simply have been a bad night.

items.prompt: The writer thinks online reviews can be useful.

explanation.en: “They can be genuinely helpful” — “useful” = “helpful” → YES. The writer’s caution does not cancel this.
explanation.kk: «They can be genuinely helpful» — «useful» = «helpful» → YES. Автордың сақтығы бұл бағаны жоққа шығармайды.
explanation.ru: «They can be genuinely helpful» — «useful» = «helpful» → YES. Осторожность автора не отменяет этой оценки.

items.quote: Those who had an average experience rarely bother
items.prompt: The writer believes customers who had an average experience often write reviews.

explanation.en: The writer says: “Those who had an average experience rarely bother” — such customers seldom write reviews. “Often” is the opposite of “rarely” → NO.
explanation.kk: Автор: «Those who had an average experience rarely bother» — мұндай клиенттер пікірді сирек жазады. «Often» сөзі «rarely» дегенге қарама-қарсы → NO.
explanation.ru: Автор пишет: «Those who had an average experience rarely bother» — такие клиенты редко пишут отзывы. «Often» противоположно «rarely» → NO.

items.quote: I doubt that they catch them all
items.prompt: The writer is confident that websites remove all fake reviews.

explanation.en: “I doubt that they catch them all” — the writer doubts it rather than being confident → NO.
explanation.kk: «I doubt that they catch them all» — автор сенімді емес, күмәнданады → NO.
explanation.ru: «I doubt that they catch them all» — автор сомневается, а не уверен → NO.

items.quote: Some businesses pay for positive comments
items.prompt: The writer thinks businesses that buy fake reviews should be fined.

explanation.en: The writer says some businesses buy reviews but says nothing about punishing them → NOT GIVEN.
explanation.kk: Автор кейбір компаниялар пікір сатып алатынын айтады, бірақ жаза туралы ештеңе айтпайды → NOT GIVEN.
explanation.ru: Автор сообщает, что некоторые компании покупают отзывы, но о наказании ничего не говорит → NOT GIVEN.

items.quote: My own approach is to look for patterns rather than individual comments
items.prompt: The writer suggests paying attention to comments that many people repeat.

explanation.en: The writer’s approach is to “look for patterns rather than individual comments”: if twenty people say the same thing, it is probably true → YES.
explanation.kk: Автордың тәсілі — «look for patterns rather than individual comments»: бір нәрсені жиырма адам жазса, бұл шындыққа жақын → YES.
explanation.ru: Подход автора — «look for patterns rather than individual comments»: если одно и то же пишут двадцать человек, это, скорее всего, правда → YES.

groups.instruction: Questions 1–5. Look at the text. Do the following statements agree with the views of the writer? Write YES if the statement agrees with the views of the writer, NO if the statement contradicts the views of the writer, or NOT GIVEN if it is impossible to say what the writer thinks about this.
